resources.string: A fixed safety answer about carbon monoxide indoors.
Can I run my portable generator in the attached garage if I keep the door open?
Is it safe to use a camping stove inside the tent to cook?
Can we bring the propane heater into the camper overnight?
Headache, dizziness, nausea or confusion near a fuel-burning device, or a CO alarm going off, even without symptoms? Get everyone into fresh air now and call emergency services.
Can I run my portable generator in the attached garage if I keep the door open?

No. Carbon monoxide (CO) from a generator […] is a poison you can\'t see or smell, and it can kill in minutes. Never run them inside a home, garage, carport, basement, shed, tent or camper, even with the doors or windows open: that is not enough ventilation. Run a generator outside only, at least 20 feet (6 metres) from any door, window or vent…

• It answers, without the model, when you plan to run a fuel-burning device indoors: a generator, a charcoal or gas grill, a camping stove or lantern, or a fuel heater in a home, garage, carport, basement, shed, tent or camper; an engine running in a garage; a gas oven or stove to heat a home; how far a generator must be from doors, windows and vents.
• The answer is always the same reviewed text, with its sources (CDC, US CPSC, NHS) and an emergency number.
• It starts with “No.” only when you ask whether you can do it.
• Why it exists: small models told people a generator in a garage was fine with the door open.
• Left to the model: electric heaters, installed and vented appliances, a propane stove in a kitchen.
• Headaches, dizziness or an alarm going off are a health question, and BOAR answers them as one.
• Questions in English, Portuguese or Spanish.
• Based on r4to's CO hazard check (BOAR R&D).
